correctness.rationale: A finite nilpotent associative ring gives a genuine two-sided brace, with lambda_A(B)=B+AB. As A ranges over R, the orbit of B is B+RB and has size \(q^{\operatorname{rank}L_B}\). The independent input rows of A produce arbitrary independent linear combinations of later rows of B, yielding rank L_B=sum_{j=2}^n dim span(rows j..n of B). A new row j in a coordinate space of dimension n-j either belongs to the old d-dimensional span in exactly \(q^d\) cases or extends it in \(q^{n-j}-q^d\) cases; row 1 is unrestricted. Thus the transition counts all matrices and gives orbit multiplicities after exact division by \(q^s\). The maximal-rank and zero-rank counts, collision probability and fixed-n asymptotic follow by elementary algebra. A standalone direct multiplication/Gaussian-elimination checker exhaustively matches predicted element-rank histograms in seven (n,q) cases, including q=4, and enumerates full action orbits in four smaller cases. Tested finite cases are not substitutes for the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Exact indecomposable-component structure is intrinsic to a finite nondegenerate involutive Yang–Baxter solution. Recent 2026 work explicitly studies component probabilities but does not make the full-size spectrum a tautological datum. The theorem classifies component sizes and multiplicities for all strict triangular matrix orders over all finite fields via a finite recurrence, proves exact extremal multiplicities and fixed points, gives a closed polynomial in the first nontrivial dimension, and derives a same-component collision probability and its high-field asymptotic. These statements are not an arbitrary finite slice, a mere existence or normalization check, or a direct rewording of the background correspondence from rings to braces. Novelty of the distribution remains subject to full-text historical verification.
